idiom_name: Slick DBIO actions composed and run with .transactionally
implementation_notes: Slick is not a tracking unit of work: DBIOAction values describe sequences that execute strictly sequentially in a single database session, and .transactionally forces the whole composed action into one transaction with a pinned session, so it either succeeds or fails atomically - that is the flush half of the pattern, while the register half stays explicit because there is no identity map or dirty checking. Doobie is the same idea in the pure-functional idiom: ConnectionIO programs are values, and a Transactor runs one in a single transaction when it is passed to .transact(xa), so composition is the unit of work and rollback is the natural consequence of a failed effect.
pitfalls: Without .transactionally every action runs in auto-commit mode, so composing actions does not make them atomic.
Only the outermost transactionally creates a transaction; nested ones run inside it without savepoints, so error recovery inside the block can leave the outer transaction marked for rollback.
DBIO actions are composed eagerly and can be executed more than once if reused, which duplicates writes.
Streaming inside a transaction can fail after elements were delivered if the commit fails; subscribers see the failure, consumers may already have acted on the data.

variants.name: doobie ConnectionIO program run by a Transactor
variants.implementation_notes: doobie builds programs as values: a ConnectionIO describes statements, and Transactor.transact runs one program in a single transaction, committing on success and rolling back on failure. Composition (flatMap, for-comprehensions) is therefore the unit of work, and because the program is a value it can be composed, reused and tested without a database. There is still no identity map or dirty tracking - statements are explicit - so the pattern's register half remains application code.
pitfalls: A program that is transacted twice executes its statements twice; keep programs as values and transact once at the boundary.
Connection management is the Transactor's job - mixing raw JDBC calls into a ConnectionIO defeats the atomicity the transactor provides.
